description: ED stated that suspects arranged approximately 500 mule bank accounts.
ED reported approximately ₹719 crore in credits through the mule-account network.
ED reported 26 cryptocurrency accounts on WazirX linked to mule accounts.
ED stated that the 26 crypto accounts facilitated cross-border crypto remittances of ₹115.67 crore to foreign wallets.
ED stated that more than 400 mule accounts were used in the earlier stage described in its release.
ED stated that ₹230.92 crore generated through the scam was integrated through more than 400 mule accounts.
ED reported freezing ₹123.58 crore in various bank accounts during searches/investigation.

scope: Nium India remittance channel mentioned in ED Jan 2025 release
description: ED described a Nium India channel through which a large amount was remitted and alleged reporting-compliance lapses. This metric must not be interpreted as the criminal proceeds amount without source context.

scope: person-specific figure in court-recorded prosecution material
description: The Kerala High Court judgment records prosecution material alleging that Sayid provided/managed 289 mule bank accounts through named contacts.

scope: person-specific figure in court-recorded prosecution material
description: The judgment records an allegation that 154 bank accounts were opened through Nitin Varghese in several banks.
The judgment records prosecution material alleging that ₹121 crore collected from victims was ultimately traced to four foreign wallets.
The judgment records an allegation that Sayid arranged crypto accounts and remitted ₹3.47 crore to four foreign wallets.
ED alleged Sayid received ₹2 crore for arranging mule bank/crypto accounts.
ED alleged Varghese received ₹70 lakh for arranging mule bank/crypto accounts.
